disclaimer: Unofficial training aid. Not an official Army product. The publication is the authoritative source; read it before acting.

slides.title: Fire Support and Field Artillery Operations
slides.subtitle: FM 3-09 (12 August 2024), chapter 2 dry run: key ideas for junior Soldiers

blurb.text: Fire support (FS) works as a system with three parts: command and control, target acquisition, and attack and delivery.

slides.title: Three parts of the fire support system

points.text: The people, command posts and networks that direct fires.
The ground force commander is responsible for command, control and coordination of fire support.
Detect, identify and locate a target well enough to engage it.
Ranges from Soldiers who see the target to advanced electronic sensors.
Cannon, rocket and missile systems, plus mortars in maneuver units.
Also air, naval, cyberspace and space capabilities.

talking_points.text: Your unit's commander controls its own fire support assets but has limited control over outside ones.

slides.title: Fire support people at company and platoon

duties.text: Fire support representative for the maneuver platoon.
Main job: locate targets accurately, then call for and adjust fire support.
The FO must fully understand their part in the observation plan.
Senior enlisted assistant to the company fire support officer; does that officer's duties when they are absent.
Trains the fire support team and the forward observers.
Works for the company or troop commander in combat.
Writes the fire support plan from the commander's guidance and submits it for approval.
A certified Service member who requests, controls and adjusts surface-to-surface fires.
Cannot control close air support attacks and does not replace a joint terminal attack controller (JTAC).

statement.text: Each maneuver company or troop gets a field artillery team that plans and coordinates all the fires supporting it.

points.text: Those fires include mortars, field artillery, naval surface fire support and close air support (CAS).
The FIST works closely with the battalion and brigade fire support elements.
Infantry and armor company FISTs make artillery, mortar and joint fire support work for the maneuver force.
Targets must meet accuracy and timeliness requirements for engagement.
Suspected targets must be confirmed before any engagement.

talking_points.text: Target selection standards are the criteria used to decide whether enemy activity is a target.

slides.title: Ground and naval fire support at a glance

cells: Firing signature can give away the unit
Large volume of fire in a very short time
High flight path: close coordination with air planners
High-angle, high rate of fire, close support
Flat trajectory is hard to adjust on flat terrain

items.text: Its firing signature makes the unit easier for enemy sensors to detect.
It has limited ability to defend itself against ground and air attack.
It has limited ability to hit moving targets well.

talking_points.text: Units must be aware that field artillery units have these built-in limits.

items.text: This is the Army's field manual for fire support and field artillery operations. Read chapter 2 before acting.
For forward observer duties see ATP 3-09.30; for FIST and fire support sergeant duties see ATP 3-09.42.
